headline: Arizona's 'Standing-Up Rocks' Now a National Park
meta_description: Chiricahua National Park in Arizona officially preserves Apache heritage and volcanic rock spires formed 27 million years ago.
summary_short: Arizona has elevated Chiricahua from national monument to national park, protecting Apache homeland and spectacular rhyolite rock formations in southeastern Arizona.
body:
After a decade of legislative effort, the United States has officially established Chiricahua National Park in southeastern Arizona, transforming a landscape of dramatic volcanic rock spires into protected federal land. The park, known locally as the 'Land of Standing-Up Rocks,' now safeguards 12,000 acres of the Chiricahua Mountains while honoring the deep cultural legacy of the Chiricahua Apache people who called this region home for thousands of years. The distinctive rock formations themselves—towering rhyolite spires and balanced boulders—were sculpted by an ancient volcanic eruption approximately 27 million years ago, creating a natural wonder that attracts hikers, climbers, and stargazers from across the country.

Chiricahua's path to national park status began when Arizona's congressional delegation introduced legislation in 2020. The area had enjoyed protection as a national monument since 1924, but the recent upgrade reflects growing recognition of both its ecological and cultural significance. Beyond the Apache heritage preserved within its boundaries, the park also protects the Faraway Ranch, a historic homestead representing the region's early settler families. Located 90 miles east of Tucson, the park sits at a remarkable ecological crossroads where desert, grassland, and forest ecosystems converge, creating habitat for diverse wildlife and vegetation across varied elevations.

Visitors can now explore the park through camping, scenic driving routes, and trails across the Sulphur Springs Valley. The designation ensures that this geological marvel and cultural touchstone will remain protected for future generations to experience and study. For those planning a visit, current information is available at NPS.gov/chir.
quick_facts: Arizona's Chiricahua elevated from national monument to national park this month
12,000 acres of volcanic rock spires in southeastern Arizona now protected
Rock formations sculpted by volcanic eruption roughly 27 million years ago
Located 90 miles east of Tucson, halfway to Las Cruces, New Mexico
Apache cultural heritage and historic Faraway Ranch preserved within park boundaries
